summary: Contract talks between BU and BUGWU began in July 2023.
Some BUGWU members went on strike in March 2024; the seven-month strike, the longest in BU's history, ended with ratification in October 2024.
BUGWU members ratified their first contract on October 16, 2024, 87% in favor and 13% against.
The National Labor Relations Board certified BUGWU as the bargaining representative in Case No. 01-RC-305360, on which the University's recognition of the union rests.
note: The agreement gives no date for the certification or the election behind it.

summary: Brown recognizes GLO as the exclusive bargaining representative of its Graduate Student Employees, as certified by the American Arbitration Association on December 6, 2018.
Bargaining for GLO's next contract began in February 2023; the union announced a first session between its bargaining committee and Brown's administration for Wednesday, February 15, 2023.

The previous (2020) agreement was due to expire on June 30, 2023; on June 28, Brown said the sides remained far apart and no successor or extension was expected by then, although bargaining had been under way since February.
In mid-November 2023 GLO and Brown reached agreement on stipends and on discrimination and harassment clauses, a breakthrough in talks that began in February.
note: The Herald article is dated Wednesday, November 22, 2023, so "last Wednesday" is November 15.

summary: GLO members voted electronically on whether to ratify the tentative agreement; voting opened December 11 and ran through midnight on Monday, December 18, 2023.
note: The post does not report the result.

summary: Bargaining for a successor contract began in February 2026. GLO opened with a 12% base stipend increase for FY27 (a $58,462 stipend), then 11% in FY28 and 10% in FY29; Brown countered with a 6.7% stipend increase over five years, which the union describes as a 0% raise in the first year.
Graduate fellows sought union recognition in March 2026 under a new Rhode Island law covering all graduate students; Brown declined to recognize them voluntarily on April 13, 2026.
The 2023 agreement expired at 11:59 pm on June 30, 2026, with bargaining for its successor still under way.

The union is recognized as exclusive bargaining representative for wages, hours and working conditions of employees in the unit the NLRB certified in Case No. 02-RC-143012. The clause names the union Graduate Workers of Columbia-UAW.
note: The agreement gives no certification date.

summary: The graduate-student workers first walked off their research, teaching and administrative jobs on March 15.
note: The article gives no year and no end date for this walkout.

summary: A 10-week strike by graduate instructors and others ended on January 7, 2022, the day after the two sides reached a tentative agreement.
note: The start date is not given in the sources.

summary: Union members voted 97 percent in favor of ratifying the contract, according to a January 28 email from the provost.
The University announced that CGSU-UE members and the University had ratified the first collective bargaining agreement.
PSC-CUNY members ratified the 2023-2027 agreement, 90% of those voting in favor, with 66% of eligible members voting over three weeks; the chancellor announced the result on January 14, 2025.
PhD students voted to unionize in an NLRB election, 1,000 to 131 (88% voting yes).
note: The date is that of the vote count reported by The Chronicle the same day.

summary: After almost two years of bargaining, the union's bargaining committee reached a full tentative agreement with the Duke administration.
Union members ratified the first contract, with 99% of those voting in favor.
note: The page is the union's Ratification 2025 page; only union members could vote.

summary: A three-day strike in 2021 preceded the ratification of the 2021 agreement.
note: The source gives the year only.

summary: The 2021 agreement was ratified in 2021, following a three-day strike.
note: The source gives the year only. Harvard's bargaining page refers to the ratification of both a 2020 and a 2021 contract with HGSU-UAW.

summary: Bargaining for a successor to the 2021 agreement began in March 2025; by October 9, 2026 the parties had held 36 formal and six informal sessions without reaching a contract (Harvard's account).
HGSU-UAW members approved a strike authorization vote in late March 2026.
Strike from April 21 to June 1, 2026, which the union ended without a collective bargaining agreement.

Harvard's August 2026 compensation proposal (not agreed): a single RA minimum for all disciplines, 6.1% on ratification (RA minimum $51,972), then 2.5% on July 1, 2027 and 2028 and 2.75% on July 1, 2029, with PhD Teaching Fellows raised to parity with RAs; hourly minimum $22.50 on ratification rising to $24.00 by July 1, 2029.
note: A proposal only, so no rates are recorded for it.

summary: HGSU-UAW members approved a second strike authorization vote in October 2026.
About 3,200 PhD student workers voted in a union election and chose TRU-UE to represent them in collective bargaining with the university.
note: The dates come from the headline summaries of two JHU Hub stories listed beside the ratification article, published January 23, 2023 (announcing the election on January 30 and 31) and February 1, 2023 (reporting the result). The vote tally is not given.

summary: Union-represented PhD students voted to ratify the three-year agreement, whose terms had been reached on March 29, 2024, after more than 40 bargaining sessions that began in May 2023.
MIT graduate workers voted overwhelmingly to unionize in April 2022 (union's account).
MIT recognizes the Union as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for graduate students employed to provide instructional or research services (RAs, TAs and instructor Gs).
note: The agreement gives no recognition date.

summary: The union kicked off negotiations for its first MIT contract with a rally on September 12, 2022.

Strike threat, not a strike: the union's account is that after it publicly announced a strike plan, and 24 hours before it was due to launch a public strike pledge, it won a tentative agreement on its first contract.
The union reports ratifying its first contract by Friday, September 22, 2023, ending a 12-month negotiation with MIT.
MIT and the union began bargaining a successor contract on April 24, 2026; five sessions had been held by June 4, 2026.

In late May 2026 MIT offered a 12-month contract extension with an immediate 3% raise for all union members; on June 1 the union declined it at the bargaining table without putting it to members (MIT's account) and proposed a 3-month extension, which MIT rejected.
note: The letter is dated Thursday, June 4, 2026, so the Monday on which the union declined the offer was June 1.

summary: MIT's letter reports that the 2023 agreement expired on May 31, 2026 and that most of its terms remain in effect until a new contract is signed.

On October 7, 2026 MIT and the union held a thirteenth negotiating session toward a new contract; the union presented a comprehensive proposal package and tentative agreements were reached on grievance procedure, nondiscrimination, workload and childcare. No successor agreement existed.
UCAN members ratified the GSRE and adjunct agreements in a vote ending January 30, 2024, with more than 99 percent of those voting in favor.
note: Dated from the union's account, which says the vote ended Tuesday, January 30. NJIT's Human Resources page says the agreement was ratified on January 31, 2024, and Patch, reporting February 1, dates the vote to Wednesday (January 31); the union may have announced the result the day after the vote closed.

summary: The 2022-2026 agreement expired June 30, 2026, without a successor.

As of October 2026, UCAN and NJIT were bargaining successor contracts for July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2030, about to take up pay, health insurance, and other economic issues; the next GSRE session was set for October 21, 2026.
The University recognizes NUGW-UE as exclusive bargaining agent under the NLRB's Certification of Representation in Case No. 13-RC-307313.
note: The agreement gives no certification date.

summary: Graduate workers ratified their first collective bargaining agreement in March 2024, after months of negotiations; the University dates ratification to March 15, 2024.
GSOC first won recognition in 2001, the first graduate union at a US private university.
A three-week strike, beginning Monday, April 26, 2021, after nearly a year of bargaining, preceded the 2020-2026 agreement.
note: Washington Square News reported on April 29, 2021 that the strike entered its third day on Wednesday, April 28, with picketing every day since Monday, which dates its start to April 26. No cited source gives the date it ended.

summary: Members ratified the agreement with a 99% yes vote on June 6, 2021.
GSOC moved from UAW Local 2110 to UAW Local 7902, which also represents NYU's contract faculty, after a membership-wide vote.
The agreement ran through August 31, 2026; either party could request successor negotiations from April 1, 2026.

Bargaining for a successor agreement was under way by the end of May 2026 (the June 1 update reports the second session). The October 7, 2026 update, after the 11th session, reports a tentative agreement on the Posting article and continuing talks on other articles.
note: None of the updates reports a full tentative agreement or any agreed pay figures.

summary: CGE-UAW petitioned the PLRB on December 4, 2024; on-site voting ran October 21 (Hershey) and October 27-29, 2025 (University Park), plus mail ballots, and the November 13, 2025 count gave 1,882 votes for CGE-UAW and 198 for no representative, of 2,241 ballots cast; 156 ballots were challenged and 5 were void.
note: The union's website reports 98 "no" votes; the Board's count is 198.

summary: Preliminary certification: the PLRB issued a nisi (preliminary) order certifying CGE-UAW as exclusive representative of graduate assistants serving as teaching, research, or administrative support assistants, to become final absent exceptions within 20 days.
Penn State filed exceptions with the PLRB challenging only the inclusion of research assistants in the unit; it said it would begin negotiating for teaching and administrative support assistants.
note: No PLRB decision or contract appears in the sources as of October 2026.

summary: The University recognizes the union as the exclusive bargaining representative of Graduate Workers under the NLRB certification in Case No. 04-RC-327396.
GETUP-UAW Local 5124 members ratified the first contract.
The University and GETUP-UAW reached a tentative agreement setting a $49,000 minimum annual stipend and a $25 minimum hourly rate.

Graduate students rejected unionization with Princeton Graduate Students United (PGSU), which intended to affiliate with UE, 652 to 391 (63% against), in an NLRB election held May 13 and 14, 2024. About half of graduate students were eligible: those titled "assistant in instruction" or "assistant in research", primarily in the natural sciences and engineering.

Bargaining for a successor to the 2022-2026 agreement (proposed by the union as a 2026-2030 agreement) began with the union's opening proposals on March 25, 2026 and was still under way at the October 8, 2026 session. The union's FAQ on graduate funding, written during bargaining, said its TA/GA article proposal had not reached tentative agreement.
SGWU members ratified their first contract with Stanford.
Graduate students were scheduled to vote on unionizing with GSU-UE in an election on January 31 and February 1, 2023.
note: The Chicago Maroon article, published January 22, 2023, gives the scheduled dates before the vote; it does not report the result. The NLRB certified the unit on March 24, 2023.

summary: The NLRB certified the graduate student employee bargaining unit in Case No. 13-RC-307974; the agreement's recognition clause also cites a second certification, Case No. 13-RC-335852.
Negotiations on a successor to the 2023-2026 agreement began November 14, 2025, with a mediator from the Michigan Employment Relations Commission that the university had requested.

Graduate Student Research Assistants voted to join the GEO bargaining unit in an election run by the Michigan Employment Relations Commission, 299 to 25 (six spoiled ballots), with 17% of the 1,910 eligible voters casting ballots.
The 2023-2026 agreement reached its May 1, 2026 end date without a successor; under Article XXVI it continues in force unless either party gives 30 days' notice of termination.

Citing slow progress, the university asked the Michigan Employment Relations Commission to begin fact-finding; by September 18, 2026 the university had offered 2.5% a year over four years and GEO 9% a year (or CPI, if higher) over three years.
At the twenty-fourth negotiation session, GEO rejected the comprehensive package the university had proposed on September 18, 2026, and continued to present individual proposals.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).
Underpaid@UT, a graduate student pay campaign organized since 2016, decided to unionize.
The UT Graduate Workers Union was founded, UT Austin's first grassroots labor union.
UW and UAW Local 4121 reached a tentative agreement on the successor contract after mediated sessions with a Public Employment Relations Commission mediator.
Members ratified the 2024-2027 agreement; UW announced it on May 23, 2024, and the contract took effect May 19, 2024, the ratification date under Article 39.
Graduate and professional workers voted to form a union in early 2023, with 91 percent of the vote.
Local 33 members ratified the first contract 1,705 to 10 in a vote held December 15 and 16, 2023; Article 38 makes it effective on ratification, December 16.
